title: Run code when an object is no longer used
objective: Write a before last reference disappears clause in a class, so the object runs a line of code when the program no longer refers to it.

body.text: Some objects hold a resource that must be cleaned up, such as a file or a connection. Inside a class, write before last reference disappears, then indent the lines to run. Lagom runs them once no name in the program still refers to the object. In these examples the message comes after the last line that uses the object, so it prints last.

body.title: A message when the object is released
body.code:
class document
    before last reference disappears
        say "document released"

make d equal to a new document
say "created"
say "finished"

body.text: The clause can use the object's fields, the same way a method can. Here the file handle keeps its name, and the clause uses it to say which file was released.

body.title: Use a field in the clause
body.code:
class file handle
    has name of type text
    before last reference disappears
        say "file released"

make f equal to a new file handle with name "x"
say "opened"
say "done"

body.prompt: The program prints created and then the release message, but the done message is missing. Make it print created, done and document released.
body.starter:
class document
    before last reference disappears
        say "document released"

make d equal to a new document
say "created"
body.solution:
class document
    before last reference disappears
        say "document released"

make d equal to a new document
say "created"
say "done"

checks.description: It prints created, done, then document released
